description: How the enterprise architecture stakeholders relate to each other: who charters and funds the practice, who models and assesses for whom, and which evidence flows steer investment, transformation, and risk decisions.

relationTypes.name: Commercial
relationTypes.description: Chartering and mandating architecture work across the enterprise

relationTypes.name: Operational
relationTypes.description: Day-to-day modeling, assessment requests, and governance routines

relationTypes.name: Financial
relationTypes.description: Budget allocation and transformation funding decisions

relationTypes.name: Information
relationTypes.description: Architecture evidence, impact assessments, and risk reporting

relations.name: Charters the EA practice
relations.description: Mandates the enterprise architecture practice with a clear remit: keep a trusted model of the estate and make simplification and modernization decisions defensible.

relations.name: Sets standards and assigns domains
relations.description: Assigns architects to business and technology domains and sets the metamodel, modeling standards, and governance routines they work within.

relations.name: Feeds domain models into the blueprint
relations.description: Maintains application, capability, and technology relationships for assigned domains and feeds them into the living enterprise model, backed by integrated operating data.

relations.name: Advises portfolio rationalization
relations.description: Delivers evidence-backed rationalization recommendations — overlap, technical debt, lifecycle risk — that the CIO uses to defend simplification and investment choices.

relations.name: Allocates transformation funding
relations.description: Steers transformation funding to the portfolio leader against architecture reality, shifting budget when roadmaps and estate evidence diverge from the plan.

relations.name: Requests capability roadmaps
relations.description: Asks the EA practice to translate strategic themes into capability roadmaps and to expose cross-program dependencies before sequencing major change.

relations.name: Delivers change impact assessments
relations.description: Assesses which applications, interfaces, and capabilities a proposed change touches and hands the impact picture to transformation planning before approval.

relations.name: Requires control traceability
relations.description: Requires architects to keep risk-relevant attributes current — control mapping, data flows, AI system inventory — so audits and exceptions can be answered from the model.

relations.name: Supplies risk and standards evidence
relations.description: Provides standards compliance status, lifecycle and resilience evidence, and AI governance posture from the architecture model for audit and regulatory reporting.

relations.name: Reports technology risk posture
relations.description: Reports control coverage, policy exceptions, and critical-system risk to the CIO, shaping which remediation and modernization work gets prioritized.

relations.name: Reports transformation progress
relations.description: Reports roadmap execution, dependency conflicts, and capability progress back to the CIO so funding and sequencing decisions stay grounded in delivery reality.
